Hip-to-Gable Loft Conversion in Wandsworth

A hip-to-gable loft conversion in Wandsworth suits the borough's end-of-terrace, semi-detached and detached houses, where the roof slopes away at the side and squeezes the loft. Building the side wall up to the ridge gives you the width for a staircase and a proper double bedroom.

Local knowledge

Where Hip-to-Gable Conversions Work in Wandsworth

Unlike the outer London suburbs, Wandsworth has relatively few streets made up entirely of hipped-roof semis. Most of its housing is Victorian and Edwardian terraces. Hipped roofs here tend to appear on the end house of a terrace, on Edwardian and interwar semi-detached pairs in Southfields, Putney and the Earlsfield borders, and on larger detached houses near the commons.

That makes each Wandsworth hip-to-gable a little different, because the gable has to sit comfortably against the rest of the terrace or its matching pair. The council has approved this kind of work: for example, a hip-to-gable roof with rear roof extensions on Gressenhall Road in Southfields.1 Where one half of a semi-detached pair converts, we pay close attention to how the new gable reads against the untouched half next door.

Planning in Wandsworth

Planning a Hip-to-Gable in Wandsworth

  • Permitted development: a hip-to-gable counts towards the 40 cubic metre (end-of-terrace) or 50 cubic metre (semi-detached) volume limit, and is exempt from the 20 cm eaves set-back.2
  • Conservation areas: roof extensions need planning permission. On estates with Article 4 directions, such as Totterdown Fields in Tooting, changes to roofs are specifically controlled.3
  • Lawful development certificate: recommended even when no application is needed, so a future buyer's solicitor has proof.

What's included

Your Wandsworth Hip-to-Gable, Start to Finish

We handle the survey, drawings, structural design, planning or lawful development certificate, party wall notices, the gable and dormer build, and building control sign-off. Our main hip-to-gable loft conversion page covers the full process and typical London costs.

The gable wall itself can be finished in render, matching brick or tile hanging. On Wandsworth's Edwardian end-of-terrace houses, where the side wall is often visible from a junction, we choose the finish that blends with the street, and we include the cost of that finish in your fixed quote rather than leaving it as a later extra.

FAQ

Wandsworth Hip-to-Gable FAQs

Does Wandsworth approve hip-to-gable conversions?

Yes, where the house and street suit it. Wandsworth has granted planning permission for a hip-to-gable roof with rear roof extensions on Gressenhall Road in Southfields, for example. Outside conservation areas, many hip-to-gable conversions are permitted development and need no application at all.

My house is mid-terrace. Can I have a hip-to-gable?

No. A hip-to-gable needs a sloping side roof, which only end-of-terrace, semi-detached and detached houses have. A mid-terrace house usually suits a rear dormer, L-shaped dormer or mansard instead.

Will I need a party wall notice for a hip-to-gable in Wandsworth?

On a semi-detached or end-of-terrace house, the new steels usually bear onto the wall you share with your neighbour, which needs at least two months' notice under the Party Wall etc. Act 1996.
